chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari narrated to me from his father, from Ahmad ibn Abi 'Abdillah Al-Barqi, from his father, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from some of our companions, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Among the rulings which are reserved (in the Knowledge of Allah) is establishing prayers in full form in four locations: in Makkah, in Madinah, in the Mosque of Kufah, and in the Ha'ir.

key_terms.الْحَائِرِ: The Ha'ir (area surrounding the shrine of Imam Husayn)

ai.seo_question: Which four locations require travelers to pray full prayers according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* establishes the Ha'ir as a distinct holy site (Mawatin) where the prayer of a traveler is completed in full (4 rak'ats), elevating the shrine of Imam Husayn to the same jurisprudential status as Makkah, Madinah, and Kufah. This ruling underscores the spiritual significance of visiting the Imams' shrines, treating them as places of residence rather than mere transit points, thereby encouraging devotees to perform complete prayers during their ziyarat.
